extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers, creative-writing students, and instructors
extracted.subtask_description: A method for writing fiction that prioritizes accessing the unconscious/dream-state and rendering scenes through sensory detail so the protagonist's yearning drives voice and narrative. Emphasizes method-writing practices (meditative preparation, body-as-instrument) over intellectualized plotting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source: access the unconscious / dream-state
rubrics_metrics.description: "Art does not come from the mind. Art comes from the place where we dream." Fiction writing must originate from the unconscious, sense-laden dream-state rather than intellectual planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter a meditative, dreamspace before drafting; get out of your head and into the world the unconscious provides. Avoid relying on planning grids or intellectual blueprints as primary generative tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method writing / body as instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocates 'method writing' analogous to Stanislavski's method acting: the body is an instrument and must remain supple, strong, and prepared; craft is secondary to the truth of emotional connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare the body and senses before writing (discipline/ritual, physical readiness). Prioritize authentic emotional access over technique; treat craft decisions as in service of emotional truth, not as the origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yearning as the story engine
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction's central engine is the protagonist's yearning—what characters want and cannot have. Yearning should drive the exploration of the human condition in the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the protagonist's yearning 'load-bearing' for the narrative: it should motivate scenes, choices, voice, and stakes. If the yearning is weak or incidental, the story will lack emotional thrust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense-based writing (senses as seat of emotions)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Get out of your head and into the world of the senses." All emotion is rooted in sensory experience; fiction must be rendered through the senses to feel emotionally true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Render scenes through tactile, visual, auditory, olfactory, and gustatory specifics rather than abstract labels for emotions. Avoid generic or rote setting description; use sensory detail to make emotion believable and earned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotions must be earned through sensory specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotional payoff in prose should be grounded in sensory specifics rather than assertions or authorial summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test scenes by asking whether the reader can feel the emotion via sense-based particulars. Replace statements like 'she was sad' with images, physical sensations, and concrete behavior that show the sadness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cinematic/sensual scene construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience fiction as a 'sensual, cinematic series of takes and scenes'—the writer 'shoots' each scene and the reader experiences it as visual/sensory immersion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose scenes as discrete, sensory-rich units (like film takes) focused on immediate perception and action; build the story through a sequence of such scenes rather than through exposition-heavy summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice emerges from character yearning and world
rubrics_metrics.description: A character's voice comes from their specific yearning and particular world, not from the writer's imposed stylistic choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop voice by deepening the character's wants, limitations, sensory experience, and environment. Avoid forcing a 'clever' authorial voice that contradicts or overshadows the character's inner life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid intellectualized fiction / imposed theme
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-pattern: intellectualized fiction — treating the story as 'what my story is about' or imposing themes rather than discovering them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let meaning emerge from the character's yearning and sensory action in the scene. Do not prioritize didactic authorial statements or outline-driven moralizing over felt experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic sensory description
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-pattern: rote, generic sensory or setting paint that does not connect to character or yearning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sensory detail specific to the character's perspective and emotional stakes; avoid stock images or background description that don't serve emotional truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid plot-first writing that strands character
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-pattern: prioritizing plot mechanics first in a way that leaves characters underdeveloped or unmotivated by yearning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure plot events arise from character wants and limitations. If plot drives character rather than character driving plot, the emotional core will be hollow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using dialogue as exposition vehicle
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-pattern: employing dialogue primarily to convey exposition rather than to reveal character, yearning, or sensory detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dialogue to show who characters are and what they want; avoid conversations that exist only to dump backstory or facts onto the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality tests / checklist for evaluating scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Butler's practical tests: Does each scene render in the senses? Is the protagonist's yearning load-bearing? Does the prose come from a meditative, accessed place rather than a planning grid? Are emotions earned through sensory specifics?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these explicit checks when revising: read a scene and confirm sensory rendering, verify the scene advances or reveals yearning, check whether prose arises from felt experience, and ensure emotional beats are shown not told.
